items.content_excerpt: $ONDS Impact on ETF Technical Reversals The formal launch of the $60 million XRC-M flight-performance testing contract reinforces the reality that sovereign military budgets are shifting away from minor experimental testing and into fully integrated, multi-year production paths. Historically, thematic drone baskets have experienced technical compression because the market treated small uncrewed systems as a temporary trend. By locking in long-term developmental capital for advanced, high-speed kinetic interceptors, the Pentagon is building a permanent, high-rate manufacturing baseline. As these multi-million dollar development outlays continue to feed down into component subcontractors and software developers, they provide the exact fundamental cash flows required to ultimately support an institutional volume reversal from the sector's oversold baselines.

If it slips back under, the call is done and you are out with a small bruise instead of a story. items.content_excerpt: $SPY A century-long nuclear battery, built on betavoltaic or Carbon-14 diamond technology, represents a transformative leap from chemical energy storage to continuous atomic decay, fundamentally altering how we power critical electronics by providing a uninterrupted, zero-maintenance electricity trickle for 20 to over 100 years. Unlike conventional lithium-ion cells that store energy chemically and degrade within years, nuclear batteries harness the natural decay of radioisotopes—such as Nickel-63, Tritium, or Carbon-14 from reactor graphite—emitting high-energy beta particles (fast electrons) into wide-bandgap semiconductors like synthetic diamond or silicon carbide. This impact triggers an avalanche of thousands of free electron-hole pairs per decay event, which are collected by an internal electric field to generate a continuous direct current. items.title: $NIO $TSLA $RIVN $XPEV 😂 The exchange between Elon Musk and William Li, NIO’s CEO. Li shared a video of the new Tesla Roadster performing it
items.content_excerpt: $NIO $TSLA $RIVN $XPEV 😂 The exchange between Elon Musk and William Li, NIO’s CEO. Li shared a video of the new Tesla Roadster performing its thruster-powered demonstrations and commented: “So impressive! This one we really don’t have. Kudos to Tesla.” Musk reposted it and replied sarcastically: “Thanks. We also don’t have a little table in a Tesla.” The joke refers to Chinese EV brands competing to add cabin comforts: refrigerators, rear-seat screens, folding tables, and extras that turn the car into a living room on wheels. There’s an interesting backstory. In 2018, William Li essentially said: “Whatever Tesla has, we have; what we have, Tesla doesn’t.” Eight years later, Li admits there’s something NIO still doesn’t have. Musk reminds him that Tesla doesn’t have a little table either. 😂 Two philosophies, two ways to show off an EV: one showcases a Roadster with thrusters; the other competes to offer more cabin comfort. Even CEOs can have a sense of humor about the competition. -

items.title: $NIO $RIVN $TSLA $XPEV Look at what I'm about to say. NIO isn't and won't be the Apple of the future, but—and don't take thi
items.content_excerpt: $NIO $RIVN $TSLA $XPEV Look at what I'm about to say. NIO isn't and won't be the Apple of the future, but—and don't take this literally—NIO should aim to become the Ferrari of Chinese electric cars. I know it has nothing to do with an actual Ferrari; I'm talking about brand prestige. I was just asked what it would take for NIO to reverse this trend. Not only to reach break-even, but also to strengthen its net profit, see Chinese indices reverse their bearish trend and enter a bullish phase, and have NIO give us a roadmap for its international expansion: target markets, timeline, investment, distribution, and sales targets. NIO doesn't need to establish a presence in 150 markets. It only needs to consolidate its position in 10 strong international markets, each generating 4,000 monthly sales. The roadmap I'd ask NIO to provide would have four elements: ten priority markets, a timeline for reaching scale, the investment required in each market, and delivery and profitability targets.

items.title: $NIO $RIVN $TSLA $SPCX This had been obsessing me, because Rivian traded at a P/S of 4.2x in June and now hovers around 3x, despite annual l
items.content_excerpt: $NIO $RIVN $TSLA $SPCX This had been obsessing me, because Rivian traded at a P/S of 4.2x in June and now hovers around 3x, despite annual losses exceeding $3 billion, while being a modest EV maker compared to NIO. The answer is that its 3x–4x P/S comes down to three factors: No Chinese jurisdiction, meaning no geopolitical discount. A Nasdaq listing, where the average P/S is around 6–7x. Most importantly, the 2024 Volkswagen deal, a political deal, of course. Because the US government doesn't intervene in business (yeah, right). VW agreed to invest up to $5.8 billion to integrate Rivian's electronic architecture and software into future group vehicles. Rivian provides the technology; VW, the capital and industrial scale. It's a strategic deal that lets Rivian monetize its technology beyond its own cars. In other words, given its jurisdiction, Nasdaq listing, and Volkswagen partnership, Rivian's P/S makes sense. And a correction of nearly 50% from the December highs .

Musk reminds him that Tesla doesn’t have a little table either. 😂 Two philosophies, two ways to show off an EV: one showcases a Roadster with thrusters; the other competes to offer more cabin comfort. $NIO $RIVN $TSLA $SPCX This had been obsessing me, because Rivian traded at a P/S of 4.2x in June and now hovers around 3x, despite annual losses exceeding $3 billion, while being a modest EV maker compared to NIO. The answer is that its 3x–4x P/S comes down to three factors: No Chinese jurisdiction, meaning no geopolitical discount. A Nasdaq listing, where the average P/S is around 6–7x. Most importantly, the 2024 Volkswagen deal, a political deal, of course. Because the US government doesn't intervene in business (yeah, right). VW agreed to invest up to $5.8 billion to integrate Rivian's electronic architecture and software into future group vehicles. Rivian provides the technology; VW, the capital and industrial scale.
